To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of incomplete multivariate samples for purposes of prediction is impossible, (2) the use of all of the observations of incomplete samples to construct estimators is possible under certain circumstances, and (3) the use of the incomplete sample to construct estimators of parameters of the truncated normal distribution is impossible.
The use of all of the observations from an incomplete multivariate sample can result in an improvement in the precision of estimators of parameters of the population from which the sample is drawn.

(i) the use of all of the data available from an incomplete multivariate sample is desirable for the purpose of constructing an estimator of the parameters of the multivariate population, and (ii) for the purpose of prediction, however, the use of incomplete samples is not desirable, and, in fact, the use of all the data available from incomplete multivariate sample may lead to poorer predictions than the use of complete multivariate samples.
